mots.sens: This verb means 'to remember' and implies a conscious action of God who remembers Noah and his situation. It evokes the idea of a benevolent attention and a promise of redemption. In the theological context, this emphasizes that God never forgets His promises and watches over His people, even in the darkest moments.

This term means 'wind' or 'spirit' and is often associated with the idea of vital breath. In this verse, the wind of God symbolizes His divine intervention to calm the waters, which can be understood as an act of creation and restoration. Theologically, this reminds us that God has the power to transform chaos into order.

The word 'waters' refers to the primordial element in creation, often associated with judgment and chaos. In this passage, the calming waters represent the end of divine judgment and the beginning of a new creation. This underscores God's sovereignty over the elements and His ability to restore what has been destroyed.

1.epoque: This passage is set in an ancient context, at a time when humanity was facing divine judgment due to its wickedness, and Noah was the only righteous one found by God.
1.passage: Genesis 8 describes the end of the flood and God's remembrance of Noah and the living beings in the ark, marking a turning point towards the restoration of the earth.
1.culture: In Hebrew culture, God's remembrance is a recurring theme, involving an active relationship between God and His people, where remembrance is often associated with divine action.
1.interpretation: This verse shows that God is attentive to the sufferings of His creatures and that He acts to save them. The mention of the wind indicates a divine intervention that brings peace after chaos, symbolizing hope and redemption.
1.commentaire: This passage reminds us that, even in moments of despair, God remembers us and acts for our good. It encourages us to trust in His faithfulness and His ability to restore our lives, no matter the storms we face. As believers, we can be assured that God is always at work, ready to bring peace and redemption.

mots.sens: This term refers to 'fountains' or 'depths' which can evoke the depths of the waters. In the context of Genesis, it refers to the marine depths and underground waters. Spiritually, this symbolizes God's control over the forces of nature, reminding us that He is sovereign over all that exists.

This word means 'heavens' and refers to both the celestial space and the dwelling place of God. It evokes the grandeur and majesty of divine creation. In this verse, the shutting of the heavens' floodgates indicates that God has the power to stop the rains, thus highlighting His authority over the elements.

This verb means 'to close' or 'to seal', and it implies a deliberate action of restriction or control. In this context, it shows that God made a decision to stop the flood, illustrating His sovereign will. It also emphasizes the notion of divine judgment and mercy, as God chose to end the rain.

2.epoque: This passage is set in a prehistoric context, after the flood, as Noah and his family emerge from the ark, marking a new beginning for humanity.
2.passage: In this chapter, God ends the rain that flooded the earth, signaling the end of judgment and the beginning of a new era. It is a key moment where God renews His covenant with humanity.
2.culture: At this time, natural phenomena were often perceived as manifestations of divine will. Rain and floods were signs of blessing or judgment according to ancient culture.
2.interpretation: Spiritually, this verse demonstrates that God has total control over the elements of creation. It reminds us that even in moments of chaos, God is sovereign and capable of restoring order.
2.commentaire: This passage teaches us that God, in His sovereignty, has the power to close the floodgates of heaven, encouraging us to trust in His will in our lives. In times of storm or uncertainty, we must remember that God is in control and has a plan for us, just as He had a plan for Noah and his family.

mots.sens: This word means 'waters' and refers to physical waters, but also to spiritual waters symbolizing purification and life. In the context of Genesis, it evokes divine judgment through the flood, but also the hope of renewal and restoration after the storm. Theologically, the 'waters' represent the separation between chaos and the order that God establishes in creation.

This term means 'dry' or 'arid', indicating the state of the earth after the waters recede. It highlights the return to life and fertility after destruction. Spiritually, this symbolizes God's promise to restore what has been destroyed and to give new life, a central theme in the story of redemption.

This verb means 'to become strong' or 'to strengthen', and in this context, it refers to the strength of the waters that covered the earth. It evokes God's power in judgment, but also in deliverance. Divine strength is at work to restore order and life, a reminder of God's sovereignty over creation.

3.epoque: This passage is set in an ancient context, probably around the third millennium BCE, at a time when the narratives of creation and divine judgment were essential for understanding the relationship between God and humanity.
3.passage: In this chapter, after the flood, God begins to restore the earth. The receding waters are a sign of the end of judgment and the beginning of a new era for Noah and his family, marking a turning point in the history of humanity.
3.culture: In ancient culture, waters were often perceived as a chaotic force, but also as a symbol of life. The receding waters after the flood represent a return to order and divine promise, which was fundamental for societies of the time.
3.interpretation: Spiritually, this verse emphasizes God's faithfulness to His promises. After judgment, there is always a possibility of renewal and restoration. It reminds us that even in moments of chaos, God is at work to bring peace and life.
3.commentaire: This passage teaches us that trials, although they may seem devastating, are often followed by a period of renewal. As believers, we can trust that God, in His sovereignty, works for our good, even amid the storms of life. We must be open to the restoration that God offers and the new life He promises.

mots.sens: The term 'Ararat' refers to a mountainous region, often associated with places of refuge and protection. In Hebrew, it evokes notions of height and safety, symbolizing a place where God preserves His people. Theologically, Ararat represents a new beginning after judgment, illustrating the divine grace that allows humanity to start anew.

This word means 'month' and is related to the lunar cycle that regulates the Hebrew calendar. It symbolizes renewal and God's timing, marking periods of celebration and remembrance. In this verse, it emphasizes the importance of divine timing in the plan of salvation, reminding us that God acts according to His own seasons.

The word 'yom' means 'day' and is often used to describe significant periods of time in the Bible. It can also refer to moments of divine revelation or God's intervention in history. In this verse, it highlights the precision of the divine plan and the importance of the moments chosen by God to act in the lives of His people.

4.epoque: This passage is set in a post-diluvian context, where humanity begins to rebuild after God's judgment on the earth through the flood.
4.passage: This verse marks a turning point in Noah's story, signaling the end of the flood and the beginning of a new era. It is crucial in the narrative of redemption and God's promise to humanity.
4.culture: In Hebrew culture, mountains are often seen as places of encounter with God, symbolizing stability and safety. Ararat, in particular, has become a symbol of refuge and promise in biblical history.
4.interpretation: Spiritually, the resting of the ark on the mountains of Ararat represents God's faithfulness to His promises. It also illustrates the concept of renewal, where after judgment, God offers humanity a new chance to draw closer to Him.
4.commentaire: This verse reminds us that even in times of crisis and judgment, God has a plan of redemption for His people. It encourages us to trust in His promises and seek refuge in Him, knowing that He is always faithful to His commitments. Like Noah, we are called to live in hope and prepare for the new beginning that God offers us.

mots.sens: This term means 'waters' and refers to waters in general, whether rivers, seas, or rains. In the context of creation and the flood, it evokes God's power over natural elements. Spiritually, waters can symbolize divine judgment, but also purification and renewal, as in baptism.

Meaning 'month', this word is linked to cycles of time and significant events in the life of the people of Israel. In the Bible, the month is often associated with religious celebrations and moments of spiritual renewal. Here, it marks a turning point in Noah's story, symbolizing a new beginning after judgment.

This word means 'mountains' and refers to land elevations. In the flood narrative, the appearance of the mountains is a sign of the end of the waters and the beginning of a new era. Theologically, this represents the stability and permanence of God's creation, contrasting with the temporary judgment of the waters.

5.epoque: This passage is set in a prehistoric context, during Noah's time, when the earth was under divine judgment due to the wickedness of man.
5.passage: In Genesis 8, we witness the end of the flood, a cataclysmic event that purified the earth. This verse marks the moment when the waters begin to recede, revealing the peaks of the mountains, a sign of hope and renewal.
5.culture: In Hebrew culture, mountains are often seen as places of encounter with God and refuge. Their emergence after the flood symbolizes the restoration of divine order after chaos.
5.interpretation: Spiritually, this verse reminds us that even after severe judgment, God offers a new beginning. The diminishing of the waters and the appearance of the mountains are metaphors for grace and redemption, emphasizing that God restores what He has created.
5.commentaire: This passage teaches us that even in the darkest moments, God has a plan for restoration. It reminds us that, like Noah, we can trust in God's faithfulness to lead us toward a new future, even after trials. Faith in God allows us to see beyond the storms of life and anticipate the light of a new day.

mots.sens: The word 'teva' refers to a box or chest, and in the context of the ark, it represents divine protection. The root of this word evokes the idea of safeguarding and refuge, highlighting how God preserves His people through the storms of life. Theologically, it reminds us that, just as Noah and his family were protected in the ark, we are also called to seek refuge in God during our trials.

The term 'chalôn' means window and symbolizes an opening to the outside world. In this verse, Noah's opening of the window represents an act of faith and expectation, allowing him to see the signs of the end of the flood. Spiritually, this teaches us the importance of being attentive to the signs God gives us and opening our hearts to see His will manifest in our lives.

The word 'arba'im' means forty and is often associated with periods of trial or preparation in the Bible. This number is rich in meanings, notably the time of purification and renewal. In this context, it reminds us that sometimes God calls us to go through times of waiting and patience before revealing His promises.

6.epoque: This passage is set in an antediluvian context, where humanity had been judged for its wickedness, and where God chose Noah to preserve a faithful remnant. It is a time marked by disobedience and divine judgment.
6.passage: This verse is part of the flood narrative, where Noah, after obeying God's command to build the ark, patiently waits for the waters to subside. The chapter describes God's faithfulness to Noah and the promise of renewal after judgment.
6.culture: In ancient culture, windows were often symbols of openness and communication. The act of opening a window could also signify the search for hope and new opportunities after a period of crisis.
6.interpretation: Spiritually, Noah's opening of the window can symbolize our own need to open our hearts and minds to the signs that God sends us. It invites us to be vigilant and discern the moments when God is acting in our lives, even after times of difficulty.
6.commentaire: This verse teaches us the importance of patience and faith in times of waiting. Like Noah, we are called to keep our eyes fixed on God and be ready to act when the moment of deliverance arrives. Opening the window of our hearts can allow us to see the light of God even in the darkest moments.

mots.sens: This word refers to a raven, a bird often associated with desolation and death in the Bible. In the context of Genesis 8:7, the raven symbolizes uncertainty and wandering, as it goes out and returns without finding rest. Spiritually, this can represent souls searching for truth without finding it, wandering in a world of despair.

This term means 'to dry' or 'to become dry,' and it is often used to describe a state of desolation or barrenness. In this verse, it indicates the end of divine judgment and the return to life. Theologically, this evokes God's promise to restore and renew, even after periods of judgment.

7.epoque: This passage is set in a prehistoric context, after the flood, where Noah and his family are the only survivors of humanity. It is a time marked by a new beginning for creation after a severe divine judgment.
7.passage: In Genesis 8, we witness the end of the flood and the process of restoring the earth. The chapter emphasizes God's faithfulness to Noah and the promises of renewal after destruction.
7.culture: In ancient culture, birds were often seen as messengers between heaven and earth. The raven, in particular, had an ambivalent connotation, symbolizing both death and survival, highlighting the importance of its role in Noah's narrative.
7.interpretation: The fact that the raven goes out and returns without finding rest indicates the absence of life and security on the still-flooded earth. This can be seen as a metaphor for humanity's search for peace and direction in times of crisis.
7.commentaire: This verse reminds us that even in moments of despair, God has a plan for restoration. Like the raven that searches without finding, we may sometimes feel lost, but it is essential to remember that God is at work to restore our lives. While waiting for God's promise, we must remain faithful and confident in His providence.

mots.sens: This word means 'dove' in Hebrew. The dove is often associated with peace and purity. In the biblical context, it also symbolizes the Holy Spirit, as in the baptism of Jesus. Here, the dove is an instrument of revelation of God's plan for creation after the flood.

This term means 'waters' in Hebrew. It evokes not only the physical element of water but also spiritual concepts such as purification and judgment. In the flood narrative, the waters represent God's judgment on the earth, but also the potential for renewal and life.

This word means 'earth' in Hebrew. It refers not only to the physical ground but also to the place of human and divine activity. The earth is the setting of the covenant between God and humanity, and here, it is the stage for restoration after divine judgment.

8.epoque: This passage is set after the flood, a major event that marked a turning point in human history, approximately 4000 years before our era.
8.passage: In this chapter, Noah seeks to assess the situation on the earth after the flood. The release of the dove is a symbolic act to discern the diminishing of the waters and the return to life on earth.
8.culture: In Hebrew culture, the dove is a symbol of peace and reconciliation. It is often used in rituals and sacrifices, representing innocence and submission to divine will.
8.interpretation: This verse illustrates Noah's quest for the restoration of order after the chaos of the flood. The dove, sent to explore, represents hope and the promise of renewal, as well as God's faithfulness to His promises.
8.commentaire: This passage reminds us that even in moments of judgment, God offers opportunities for renewal. Like Noah, we are called to seek God's direction in our lives, trusting that He will guide us toward times of peace and restoration. The dove teaches us to be instruments of peace in a world often troubled.

mots.sens: This word means 'dove' and evokes peace and purity. In the biblical context, the dove is often associated with the Spirit of God, as in the baptism of Jesus where the Spirit descends upon him in the form of a dove. Thus, the presence of the dove in this verse symbolizes hope and the search for the promised land after divine judgment.

The term 'waters' refers to the vital element and purification, but in this context, it also represents God's judgment on the earth through the flood. The waters cover the earth, symbolizing the destruction of evil and the necessity of a new creation. Spiritually, this reminds us that God can purify and renew, even after severe judgment.

The word 'ark' refers to the large vessel built by Noah to save his family and the animals from the flood. It symbolizes divine protection and refuge in times of crisis. Theologically, the ark represents the salvation that God offers to those who trust Him, foreshadowing the salvation that Christ brings to humanity.

9.epoque: This narrative is set in an antediluvian era, where the wickedness of man had reached its peak, prompting God to judge the earth with the flood.
9.passage: In this passage, Noah waits for the return of the dove, a symbol of hope and the possibility of new life after judgment. This chapter deals with the end of the flood and the beginning of a new era for humanity.
9.culture: In Hebrew culture, the dove is a symbol of peace and reconciliation. It is often used in rituals and sacrifices, emphasizing the importance of purity and communication with God.
9.interpretation: The dove returning to Noah without finding a place to rest illustrates the search for peace and security in a troubled world. This reminds us that even after times of judgment, God offers a new chance and renewed hope.
9.commentaire: This verse teaches us that even in the darkest moments, God is at work to bring peace and restoration. Like Noah, we must be attentive to the signs God sends us and seek to understand His will. In times of uncertainty, we can find refuge in Christ, our ark, who protects us and guides us toward new life.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to sit', 'to remain', or 'to dwell'. In the context of Genesis 8:10, it evokes the idea of waiting and patience, highlighting the importance of perseverance in trials. The root of this word is found in the idea of stability and security, which can be understood as an invitation to remain in faith even when circumstances seem uncertain.

This verb means 'to let go' or 'to release'. In this verse, it symbolizes the act of releasing the dove, representing hope and the search for peace. This word is often associated with the idea of trusting God for guidance and restoration, which is particularly relevant in the flood narrative.

This term means 'right' or 'right hand', often associated with strength and divine favor. In the context of releasing the dove, it can be interpreted as an indication of God's protection and guidance towards Noah and his family, reinforcing the idea that God is both their refuge and support in difficult times.

10.epoque: This narrative takes place after the flood, a period marked by destruction and the renewal of creation, where Noah and his family emerge from a time of confinement in the ark.
10.passage: In this chapter, God has already promised not to destroy the earth with water again. Verse 10 shows Noah's patience as he waits for the right moment to release the dove, a symbol of peace and hope.
10.culture: In Hebrew culture, the dove is often a symbol of peace and the Spirit of God. The act of releasing the dove after a period of waiting underscores the importance of patience and trust in God.
10.interpretation: This verse teaches us that waiting in faith is essential. Noah, by waiting another seven days, demonstrates trust in God's promise and a desire to see the earth restored. The released dove represents the hope of a new beginning.
10.commentaire: This passage reminds us that patience is a valuable virtue in our walk with God. Just as Noah waited for the right moment to release the dove, we are called to trust God in our own times of waiting. In times of uncertainty, we must remember that God has a plan and that He acts according to His perfect timing.

mots.sens: The word 'יונה' (dove) refers to a bird often associated with peace and purity. In Hebrew culture, the dove is also a symbol of the Holy Spirit. The root of this word evokes the idea of gentleness and tranquility, which is relevant in the context of Noah's deliverance and God's promise of renewal.

The word 'זית' (olive) refers to the tree that produces olives, a symbol of peace and prosperity. In the Bible, the olive tree is often associated with divine blessing and restoration. The olive leaf, as a sign of the receding waters, represents hope and the beginning of a new season of life after judgment.

The word 'מים' (waters) is plural and refers to the waters that submerged the earth during the flood. This term emphasizes God's power in judgment, but also His ability to restore. In a spiritual context, the waters can symbolize divine judgment, but also renewal and purification.

11.epoque: This passage is set in a pre-Abrahamic context, where humanity has been judged for its wickedness, and Noah is chosen by God to be the means of preserving life on earth.
11.passage: This verse is found in the flood narrative, where Noah sends the dove to check if the waters have receded. Chapter 8 of Genesis describes the end of the flood and the beginning of the restoration of the earth.
11.culture: In ancient culture, the dove was often used as a symbol of peace and reconciliation. The olive leaf has become a universal symbol of peace, rooted in this biblical story.
11.interpretation: The dove returning with an olive leaf indicates that God has begun to restore the earth after judgment. This symbolic gesture reminds believers that, even in moments of despair, God always offers a way toward redemption and hope.
11.commentaire: This verse reminds us that, even after times of judgment and difficulty, God is faithful to His promises of restoration. The dove and the olive leaf symbolize the hope and peace that God offers to those who trust Him. In our lives, even in times of trial, we can expect God's goodness and His benevolent intervention.

mots.sens: This word refers to the 'dove', a bird often associated with peace and the presence of the Spirit of God. In the biblical context, the dove is also a symbol of purification and reconciliation. The fact that it does not return to Noah can be interpreted as a sign of the end of divine judgment and the beginning of a new era of life on earth.

This term means 'to return' or 'to go back'. It evokes the idea of movement towards a point of origin or restoration. In this verse, the fact that the dove does not return to Noah symbolizes God's promise of a new creation and renewal, marking a break from the past of judgment and destruction.

This word means 'seven', a number that symbolizes fullness and perfection in the Bible. In the context of this verse, Noah's seven days of waiting emphasize patience and trust in God. This reminds us that sometimes, God calls us to wait to see the fulfillment of His promises.

12.epoque: This passage is set in the post-flood context, when Noah and his family emerge from the ark after the flood. It is a period of renewal and restoration of humanity after a severe divine judgment.
12.passage: Chapter 8 of Genesis recounts how Noah patiently waits for the waters to recede. The releasing of the dove is a symbolic act to assess the situation of the outside world and testifies to Noah's faith in God's promise.
12.culture: In ancient culture, the dove was often used as a symbol of peace and divine communication. The act of releasing the dove was a way to seek signs of God's will and the possibility of a new beginning.
12.interpretation: Spiritually, the fact that the dove does not return to Noah represents hope and the promise of a restored future. It shows that God opens new paths and that, even after judgment, there is a possibility of life and renewal.
12.commentaire: This verse teaches us the importance of patience and faith in our own lives. Like Noah, we are called to wait for God's promises, even when signs seem absent. The dove that does not return reminds us that God has a plan for our future, and that we can move forward with confidence toward what He has prepared.

mots.sens: This term means 'to be dry' or 'to fade away'. It evokes the idea of dryness, but also of purification and renewal. In the context of Genesis 8:13, it emphasizes the end of divine judgment through the waters of the flood and the beginning of a new era for creation, symbolizing hope and the restoration of the earth.

This word designates the flood, a cataclysmic event of divine judgment upon the earth. It is associated with God's anger against human wickedness, but also with mercy, as Noah and his family were preserved. In this verse, the mention of the end of the floodwaters underscores God's faithfulness to His promises and His desire to restore humanity.

This word means 'ark' and has connotations of protection and refuge. Noah's ark represents divine salvation in a desolate world. Spiritually, it symbolizes the salvation that God offers to those who trust Him, marking the separation between judgment and grace.

This verb means 'to see' or 'to look', implying careful observation. In this context, it highlights the importance of recognizing the signs of God's grace. Noah, by looking at the earth, testifies to God's faithfulness to His promises and the possibility of a new beginning.

13.epoque: This passage is set in a pre-flood context, where humanity had reached an extreme level of corruption, leading to divine judgment through the flood. The time of Noah is marked by disobedience and rejection of God.
13.passage: In this chapter, after the flood, God begins to restore the earth. Noah, as a new Adam, is called to observe and participate in the new creation that God initiates after the judgment.
13.culture: The culture of Noah's time was characterized by idolatrous practices and widespread immorality. The construction of the ark and the survival of Noah and his family testify to the necessity of faith and obedience to God in a declining world.
13.interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment when God's judgment comes to an end and the promise of renewal begins. It reminds us that even after periods of judgment, God always offers a way of redemption and restoration, symbolized by Noah and his ark.
13.commentaire: Genesis 8:13 teaches us that God is faithful to His promises and that there is always hope even after difficult times. By observing the dry land, Noah shows us the importance of recognizing God's works in our lives. This passage encourages us to have faith in God's ability to restore and renew, even in the darkest moments.

mots.sens: This term designates the earth, the soil, or the land. In the context of Genesis, it evokes creation and God's promise to humanity. The earth is the place where God acts and where man is called to live in communion with Him. Spiritually, the earth also symbolizes the heart of man, which must be renewed and purified by divine grace.

This word means 'dry' or 'parched'. It evokes the idea of separation from water, representing restoration after divine judgment. In a broader sense, it can symbolize the process of purification and renewal that God works in the lives of believers. Theologically, the dryness of the earth after the flood reminds us that God restores what He has created, offering a new chance to humanity.

This term means 'month' and is often associated with a new beginning or renewal. In the Hebrew calendar, each month is an opportunity to draw closer to God and celebrate His faithfulness. Spiritually, this can be seen as a symbol of rebirth and the cycles of life in faith, where each month represents a new opportunity to walk with God.

14.epoque: This verse is set in the post-flood context, where God restores the earth after the judgment of the flood, marking a new beginning for humanity.
14.passage: In this passage, Noah and his family emerge from the ark after a long wait. This moment is crucial as it symbolizes the end of judgment and the beginning of a new era of promises and blessings from God.
14.culture: In Hebrew culture, time and seasons are often perceived as cycles of divine providence. The precise mention of the date underscores the importance of chronology in the fulfillment of God's promises.
14.interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's faithfulness to His promises. After judgment, God restores the earth, reminding us that even after periods of crisis, He is capable of renewing and restoring. This encourages us to trust in His ability to transform our lives.
14.commentaire: This passage teaches us that God is a God of new beginnings. Just as the earth was restored after the flood, we too can experience restoration in our lives when we turn to Him. This calls us to live in hope and to seize each day as an opportunity for spiritual renewal.

mots.sens: This word means 'word', 'thing', or 'matter'. In the biblical context, it evokes the idea of divine communication, where God expresses Himself and reveals His will. The root of this word underscores the importance of the word as the means by which God interacts with humanity, thus highlighting the personal relationship between God and Noah.

The name 'Noah' means 'rest' or 'comfort'. It is linked to God's promise to restore and renew creation after the flood. Noah is a symbol of obedience and faith, representing those who listen to God's voice and act according to His instructions, which has profound implications for the community of believers.

15.epoque: This passage is set in a post-flood context, where humanity begins to rebuild after God's judgment on the earth. It is a period of renewal and divine promise, marked by the restoration of creation.
15.passage: In this chapter, God speaks to Noah after the flood, giving him instructions and promises for the future. This moment is crucial as it marks the beginning of a new covenant between God and humanity, symbolized by the rainbow.
15.culture: In Hebrew culture, the word of God is considered powerful and creative. Divine communication is essential for understanding God's will and living in accordance with it, which is reflected in the relationship between Noah and God.
15.interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of listening to God's voice. The divine word is a source of direction and comfort, inviting believers to submit to God's will while affirming that God remains committed to His people despite trials.
15.commentaire: This passage reminds us that God still speaks today and desires to establish a relationship with each of us. Like Noah, we are called to listen carefully to God's voice and act according to His instructions, which can lead to blessings and spiritual renewal in our lives. Let us be attentive to His word and open to His action in our daily lives.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to go out' or 'to emerge'. It evokes the idea of leaving a confined space to enter a new environment. In the context of this verse, it symbolizes deliverance and the beginning of a new life after the flood, highlighting the divine providence that allows Noah and his family to start anew. Spiritually, this can represent the exit from darkness into light, a metaphor for redemption.

This term refers to the ark, a structure designed for protection and preservation. In the Bible, the ark is a symbol of refuge and salvation, representing God's grace that preserves those who trust Him. Christian theology sees this as a foreshadowing of Christ, our ark of salvation, who protects us from judgment.

This word means 'woman' and emphasizes the importance of the marital relationship in God's plan. In this verse, it reminds us that family is at the heart of divine creation and that human community is essential for the continuity of humanity. This highlights the value of family in God's design and the importance of relationships in the kingdom of God.

This term means 'sons' and represents descent and the continuity of lineage. In the context of this verse, it underscores Noah's responsibility as a father and head of the family to pass on faith and divine values to his children. Spiritually, this evokes the idea that each generation must rise to honor God and perpetuate His legacy.

16.epoque: This passage is set in a pre-flood period, marked by corruption and violence on earth, before divine judgment through the flood.
16.passage: In this chapter, after the flood, God commands Noah to come out of the ark, marking the beginning of a new era for humanity. This moment is crucial as it symbolizes redemption and God's promise not to destroy the earth with water again.
16.culture: In Hebrew culture, family and community are fundamental values, and the fact that Noah exits the ark with his family underscores the importance of familial solidarity in times of crisis.
16.interpretation: This verse illustrates God's faithfulness to Noah and his family, offering them a second chance to live according to His ways. Spiritually, it reminds us that God calls us to come out of our trials and embrace the new life He offers us.
16.commentaire: This passage teaches us that even after times of judgment, God offers opportunities for renewal and redemption. By coming out of the ark, Noah and his family enter a new phase of their existence, prompting us to reflect on our own lives and respond to God's call to move toward a future He has prepared for us.

mots.sens: This word means 'to increase', 'to multiply', or 'to grow'. It evokes the idea of abundant growth and prosperity. In the context of Genesis 8:17, it emphasizes God's divine intention to fill the earth with life, a recurring theme in creation. Theologically, this reminds us that God desires life and the multiplication of His creatures, which testifies to His goodness and providence.

This term translates to 'species' or 'kind'. It refers to the diversity of creatures according to their category. In the verse, this underscores the divine order in creation, where each type of animal has its place and role. Spiritually, it reminds us that God has a plan for every aspect of His creation, and that diversity is an integral part of His design.

This word means 'earth' or 'land'. It represents not only the physical place but also the domain of human and divine action. In this verse, the earth is the place where the animals are to spread and multiply, highlighting the importance of the earth as God's creation. This reminds us of our responsibility to care for creation and live in harmony with it.

17.epoque: This passage is set in a post-flood context, where Noah and his family exit the ark after the flood, symbolizing a new beginning for humanity and creation.
17.passage: Genesis 8:17 is part of the account of the end of the flood, where God commands Noah to release the animals to repopulate the earth. This moment marks a key step in the renewal of creation.
17.culture: In ancient culture, animals were often seen as symbols of fertility and prosperity. Releasing the animals to multiply was an act of divine blessing and restoration of natural order.
17.interpretation: This verse illustrates God's desire to restore life on earth after judgment. It emphasizes the importance of animal life and humanity's responsibility toward creation, while announcing a future full of promises.
17.commentaire: This passage reminds us that God is the creator and restorer of all life. By calling us to care for His creation, He entrusts us with a sacred responsibility. As Christians, we are called to be stewards of the earth, promoting life and caring for all its creatures, thus reflecting God's love and goodness in our world.

mots.sens: The name 'Noah' means 'rest' or 'comfort'. It is derived from the Hebrew root 'נח' which evokes the idea of peace and respite. In the context of this verse, Noah represents not only a man of faith but also an instrument of salvation for his family, symbolizing hope and renewal after divine judgment through the flood.

The verb 'יָצָא' means 'to go out' or 'to exit'. This word carries the idea of movement and liberation, indicating a transition from a state of confinement to a new environment. Spiritually, this can symbolize deliverance and the beginning of a new life, emphasizing that Noah and his family were preserved for a new start on earth.

The term 'אִשָּׁה' designates a woman, often in relation to her role in the family. In this verse, it highlights the importance of family in God's plan. Theologically, this reminds us that family is a divine institution, essential for the continuity of humanity and the transmission of faith.

The word 'בָּנִים' means 'sons', and it is often associated with the idea of descent and heritage. In the context of Noah, this emphasizes the responsibility to pass on faith and values to the next generation. Spiritually, this underscores the importance of spiritual education within the family.

18.epoque: This passage is set in a pre-flood context, where humanity had reached an extreme degree of corruption, leading to God's judgment through the flood. Noah, as the patriarch, is chosen to preserve humanity and creation.
18.passage: Chapter 8 of Genesis describes the end of the flood and the exit of Noah and his family from the ark. This moment marks a turning point in the history of humanity, symbolizing a new covenant between God and humanity.
18.culture: In Hebrew culture, family is central and is considered the foundation of society. The exit of Noah and his family from the ark represents the continuity of humanity and the importance of family ties in fulfilling divine promises.
18.interpretation: Spiritually, the exit of Noah and his family from the ark represents the beginning of a new era after God's judgment. It also illustrates the theme of redemption and renewal, where God offers a second chance to humanity.
18.commentaire: This verse reminds us that even in moments of judgment, God preserves those who are faithful to Him. The exit of Noah and his family symbolizes hope and the promise of a new beginning. As believers, we are called to live in faith and to pass this faith on to our families, relying on God's promises for our future.

mots.sens: This term refers to 'animals' in a general sense, encompassing all living creatures. It comes from the root 'חיה' which means 'to live' or 'to be alive.' In this verse, it emphasizes the diversity of God's creation and His desire to preserve life. Theologically, it reminds us that God is the creator and sustainer of all life on earth.

This word translates as 'reptile' or 'creature that moves on the ground.' It evokes creatures that move in a crawling manner, often associated with the earth. The presence of this term in the text highlights the diversity of species that God has created. Spiritually, it reminds us that God has a plan for every aspect of His creation, even those that seem insignificant.

This word means 'bird' and refers to all winged creatures. It comes from the root 'עוף' which implies flight and lightness. In the context of this verse, it illustrates the ability of birds to rise above difficulties, symbolizing hope and freedom. Theologically, it reminds us that God has given each creature a role in His divine plan.

This term means 'according to their kinds' and emphasizes the order and diversity of creation. It comes from the root 'מין' which designates a category or type. In this verse, it highlights the fact that God created each species with a specific purpose. It reminds us that every living being has value and a role in God's design.

19.epoque: This passage is set in the post-flood context, where Noah and his family emerge from the ark after the flood. It is a time of renewal and restoration of creation.
19.passage: Genesis 8 recounts the end of the flood and the moment when Noah releases the animals from the ark. This chapter emphasizes God's faithfulness to His creation and His commitment to restore the earth.
19.culture: In ancient culture, animals were often seen as symbols of divine forces or nature. The story of Noah and the ark demonstrates God's sovereignty over all creatures and His desire to preserve life.
19.interpretation: This verse illustrates God's power which, after judgment, restores life on earth. Each species coming out of the ark represents the hope of a new beginning and the promise of the continuity of creation.
19.commentaire: This passage teaches us that God cares for all His creation and has a plan for every living being. As Christians, we are called to respect and protect God's creation, recognizing that every creature has a role in His design. The release of the animals from the ark also symbolizes renewal and hope, reminding us that despite trials, God is always at work to restore and renew.

mots.sens: This word means 'altar' and derives from the root 'zavach', which means 'to sacrifice'. In the biblical context, an altar is a place of encounter between God and man, where offerings are presented. The establishment of an altar by Noah after the flood underscores the importance of worship and the acknowledgment of divine sovereignty in the believer's life.

This term designates a 'burnt offering', an offering completely consumed by fire. The burnt offering symbolizes total devotion to God and the pursuit of purification. In this verse, Noah's offering is an expression of gratitude and devotion to God, marking a new beginning after the judgment of the flood.

This word means 'pure' and is often used to designate what is acceptable before God. The clean animals were those that could be offered in sacrifice, representing holiness and separation from sin. The use of clean animals by Noah shows his desire to draw near to God in purity and holiness.

20.epoque: This passage is set in a post-flood context, where Noah and his family are the only survivors of humanity, having been preserved by God because of their faithfulness.
20.passage: In this chapter, Noah, after leaving the ark, expresses his gratitude to God by building an altar and offering sacrifices. This marks the beginning of a new era for humanity, under God's grace.
20.culture: In Hebrew culture, sacrifice was a central act of religious life, symbolizing reconciliation with God and the expression of faith. Altars were sacred places where people could draw near to God.
20.interpretation: Noah's act of building an altar and offering burnt offerings testifies to his recognition of divine mercy and his commitment to God. It underscores the importance of worship and devotion in the relationship between man and the Creator.
20.commentaire: This verse teaches us that even after difficult times, our response to God should be gratitude and praise. Like Noah, we are called to establish 'altars' in our lives, places of encounter with God where we can offer our hearts as a sacrifice. It reminds us that each day is an opportunity to acknowledge God's goodness and to live in communion with Him.

mots.sens: This word means 'odor' or 'fragrance'. In the biblical context, it often evokes a pleasant aroma that pleases God, symbolizing acceptance and divine happiness. Here, the pleasing aroma of Noah's sacrifice represents humanity's devotion and acknowledgment of God, marking a moment of reconciliation after the flood.

This term means 'because of' or 'due to'. It emphasizes the causal relationship between human actions and divine decisions. In this verse, God declares that He will no longer curse the ground because of the evil thoughts of man, thus showing His mercy and willingness to restore creation despite humanity's sinful nature.

This word means 'heart' and represents the center of human emotions, thoughts, and intentions. In the Bible, the heart is often seen as the source of actions and desires. Here, it is mentioned to emphasize the fallen condition of humanity, but also God's grace in choosing not to destroy His creation again.

This word means 'living' or 'life'. It is fundamental in the biblical text as it refers to all that is animated by the life of God. In this verse, God commits to no longer strike everything that is living, illustrating His promise to preserve life and not repeat the judgment of the flood.

21.epoque: This passage is set after the flood, a significant event in human history, where God judged sin through destruction, but also established a new covenant with Noah and his family.
21.passage: In Genesis 8, after the flood, Noah offers a sacrifice to God, and this verse reveals God's response to that offering. God expresses His decision not to curse the ground again, thus establishing a promise of grace toward creation.
21.culture: In Hebrew culture, sacrifices were acts of devotion and acknowledgment toward God. The pleasant aroma of sacrifices symbolized divine acceptance and communion between God and man.
21.interpretation: This verse highlights God's mercy despite humanity's sinful nature. It announces a new era where God chooses not to inflict destructive judgment, but rather to maintain life and offer a chance for redemption.
21.commentaire: This passage reminds us that despite our sinful condition, God is full of grace and mercy. He chooses not to treat us according to our merits, but according to His love. As believers, we are called to live in recognition of this grace, offering our lives as a pleasing aroma to God through our actions and thoughts.

mots.sens: This word means 'seed' or 'grain.' It evokes the idea of beginning, potential, and growth. In the biblical context, it symbolizes not only physical reproduction but also God's promise to multiply His blessings. Spiritually, it reminds us that every act of faith and every word of God carries within it the potential for an abundant harvest.

This term means 'to subsist' or 'to exist.' It implies continuity and permanence over time. In this verse, it emphasizes God's faithfulness in maintaining the order of creation. Theologically, it assures us that the natural and spiritual laws established by God will remain as long as the earth exists.

This word means 'days' and refers to periods of time. In the context of this verse, it highlights the regularity of the day-night cycle. It evokes God's constancy in creation and reminds believers that each day is a new opportunity to live according to His will.

This word means 'cold' and represents climatic conditions. It is often associated with difficult times or scarcity. In this verse, it reminds us that the seasons, including cold moments, are part of the divine plan, teaching us to trust God even in times of difficulty.

22.epoque: This verse is set in the post-flood context, where God establishes a new covenant with Noah and humanity after the flood. It is a period of renewal and divine promise.
22.passage: Genesis 8:22 is found in the account of the restoration of the earth after the flood. God promises that the natural cycles will endure, thus ensuring the continuity of life on earth.
22.culture: In ancient culture, farmers depended on the seasons for their survival. This verse reaffirms the trust one can have in God for the regularity and faithfulness of His promises, which was crucial for agricultural societies.
22.interpretation: This verse underscores God's sovereignty over creation and His ability to establish natural laws that endure. Spiritually, it reminds us that despite the changes and uncertainties of life, God's faithfulness is constant, and we can rely on His promises.
22.commentaire: Genesis 8:22 encourages us to recognize God's hand in the cycles of nature and to live in trust. Each season, each day, is an opportunity to see God's faithfulness at work. As believers, we are called to sow the word of God in our lives and to wait in faith for the harvest He promises.
